boundedQuestion: How can an adapter exclusion-policy upgrade avoid silent permission inheritance without forcing unrelated anchors to migrate?

realFailure.observation: N309 proved that N308 omitted exclusions from closure identity, allowing a Producer to reclassify an observed undeclared input as unrelated after the run.
realFailure.n309Correction: N309 hashes preauthorized exclusion rules and rejects after-run additions, but leaves adapter policy migration unresolved.
realFailure.gap: Without immutable policy revisions, activation receipts, and affected-anchor replay, an adapter upgrade can silently reinterpret an old anchor under new exclusion authority or force an unnecessarily global workbench re-anchor.
realFailure.regressionDecision: Refine the existing inactive N309 regression. Do not create another regression case.

teacher.name: Open Policy Agent policy bundles, scoped roots, activation status, and decision-log revision binding
teacher.exactQuestionAnswered: How can a new policy revision be scoped, validated, activated, rolled back, and bound to each decision without overwriting unrelated policy state?
teacher.whatItKnowsBeyondCurrentBestView: N309 binds exclusion rules into one closure digest but does not define revision migration. OPA adds explicit bundle revisions and owned roots, forbids delta updates from changing roots, activates a new signed/validated bundle only after verification, retains the previous active revision on activation failure, and records the bundle revision used for each decision.

facts: Bundle manifests can declare revision and roots.
Scoped roots limit which policy/data namespace a bundle owns.
A delta bundle must keep the original roots and cannot change scope.
Verification or activation failure keeps the existing bundle active.

sources.fact: Decision-log events record the revision of each policy bundle used at evaluation time.
Status reports active_revision as the last successful activation.
The public schema requires revision and defines roots.
The repository contains executable bundle activation and status tests.
The official repository was active on 2026-11-17.

screening.sourceProvenance: Official openpolicyagent.org documentation and open-policy-agent/opa repository.
screening.maintenanceReleaseIssueActivity: Public and unarchived; multiple commits were observed on 2026-11-17 and release v1.22.4 was published on 2026-11-12.
screening.runnableCodeTestsData: Open-source Go implementation, CLI, bundle schemas, signed-bundle test data, activation tests, decision-log tests, and end-to-end tests are present.
screening.licenseAndAssetRights: Apache-2.0, LICENSE blob 8f71f43fee3f78649d238238cbde51e6d7055c82. This audition transfers a protocol principle, not third-party assets.
screening.directRelevance: Directly answers revisioned exclusion-policy activation, scope control, decision-to-policy binding, and last-known-good rollback.
screening.noveltyRelativeToCurrentBestView: Adds immutable policy revisions, scope-preserving patches, exact decision revision, affected-anchor replay, atomic activation, and rollback beyond N309's single closure hash.
screening.dependencyHardwareCostDataIntegrationRis: Full OPA integration is unnecessary and would add a Go policy runtime, Rego, bundle distribution, and signing operations. The Candidate uses only a small JSON receipt and hashes; large anchor registries make impact-set computation and replay cost nontrivial.
screening.demoOpacityClosedVersionRisk: Not demo-only, opaque, or closed; implementation, schemas, tests, documentation, releases, license, and history are public.

candidateMethod.name: Revision-Pinned Exclusion Policy Migration
candidateMethod.analogyBoundary: OPA is a method teacher. KAOPU does not adopt Rego, the OPA runtime, its network service, or its policy ontology.
rules: An existing anchor is always interpreted under the exact policy revision and digest recorded when its decision was made.
A PATCH migration may not add, remove, or widen owned input roots.
Any scope change requires a new SNAPSHOT-style policy identity plus explicit coordinator authorization.
Only anchors whose known inputs intersect changed policy rules are replayed; unrelated anchors remain pinned to their original immutable policy revision.
The new policy becomes active only after all impacted-anchor replay receipts pass and bind the exact target revision and digest.
Activation failure retains the last successful revision; no fallback is reported as a successful migration.
Producer cannot approve impact-set completeness, replay results, or activation.

stateSemantics.POLICY_MIGRATION_CANDIDATE: A new immutable policy revision and diff exist, but it is not active.
stateSemantics.HOLD_POLICY_SCOPE_CHANGE_REQUIRES_SNAPSH: A patch attempts to change exclusion authority roots.
stateSemantics.HOLD_POLICY_MIGRATION_UNREPLAYED: At least one impacted anchor lacks a replay bound to the target policy revision.
stateSemantics.HOLD_POLICY_ACTIVATION_FAILED: Authorization, validation, or replay failed; the last successful revision remains active.
stateSemantics.POLICY_REVISION_ACTIVATED: All impacted anchors passed independent replay under the exact new policy revision.
stateSemantics.LEGACY_ANCHOR_PINNED: An unaffected or not-yet-migrated anchor remains valid only under its recorded legacy policy revision.

findings: A same-scope policy revision activated only after replaying the affected Garment anchor.
The unrelated Terrain anchor required no replay and remained pinned to its original policy revision.
Adding runtime/material-override to policy roots while claiming PATCH returned HOLD_POLICY_SCOPE_CHANGE_REQUIRES_SNAPSHOT.
A scope-changing snapshot without replay returned HOLD_POLICY_MIGRATION_UNREPLAYED.
A failed replay returned HOLD_POLICY_ACTIVATION_FAILED and kept garment-exclusions/v1 active.

boundaries: Impact-set computation is only as complete as each anchor's recorded known inputs; hidden dependencies remain a separate N308/N309 risk.
Policy revision identity does not prove that an exclusion is semantically correct or user-authorized.
Mixed legacy revisions require immutable retrieval of historical policy bundles; deleting an old bundle makes its anchors unverifiable.
A scope-preserving policy text change can still alter meaning and therefore requires replay of intersecting anchors.
Large registries may need indexed input-to-anchor traceability; this Candidate does not prescribe a database or service architecture.
No production adapter, anchor registry, Mother, R2 rule, or public KaoPuGram service changes before a single-Mother trial.

decision.scope: Candidate-only; one dependency-rich Mother trial after N309 is corrected, with old policy bundle retained as rollback.
decision.rollbackPoint: Keep N309 in HOLD_GATE_FAIL and retain every anchor on its recorded policy revision if impact selection or activation replay is incomplete.
